subject: Exportable per-route cost/latency breakdown + thresholding — action plan
messages:
From: Priya Reddy <priya@edgescale.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Export for per-route cost/latency + alert thresholds

Hi Jonas —

Quick context: we're close to signing but procurement needs an exportable report that shows per-route token cost, median/tail latency, and a way to map alerts to route owners. They want: a CSV export (daily), column-level breakdown by model variant, quantization profile, and a simple thresholding UI so our SREs can subscribe to high-cost route alerts.

Can Redwood provide an out-of-the-box CSV and an API endpoint we can poll while we finalize the contract? If not immediately possible, can you share a short timeline and what would be included in the CSV schema?

Thanks — appreciate the quick turn.

— Priya
Director of Engineering, EdgeScale
attachments: none
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Priya Reddy <priya@edgescale.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Export for per-route cost/latency + alert thresholds

Priya —

Thanks, and congrats on the progress. Short answer: we can deliver a CSV export and a minimal alerting surface in the Console within a short runway, but there are trade-offs around sampling, export frequency, and the schema we can guarantee for the first drop.

Planned deliverables (initial):
- Daily CSV export with per-route rows: route_id, route_name, model_variant, quant_profile, tokens_in, tokens_out, token_cost_estimate, median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, window_start
- API endpoint to request the most recent export (authenticated, team-only)
- Console UI: simple threshold rule builder (route selector + metric + threshold + notification target)

I'm looping in Marissa (product) and Dylan (infra) to scope feasibility and timeline. If EdgeScale needs hourly exports or raw per-request logs, that's additional work — let's clarify.

Next step: Marissa—can you draft an MVP scope (1–2 weeks) and a proposed Console UX? Dylan—can you confirm whether the runtime can export the aggregated rows without adding intolerable latency to serving?

— Jonas
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Export for per-route cost/latency + alert thresholds

Jonas / team —

Technical constraints / notes from infra: we already emit per-request metrics to our telemetry pipeline, but the cardinality of route + model_variant + quant_profile + tenant can explode. For daily aggregated CSV we can rely on the existing aggregation job with these caveats:

- Aggregation window: daily end-of-day job, supports shorter windows but will increase processing cost.
- Sampling: for p99 accuracy across low-traffic routes we need full retention for the window; otherwise p99 will be noisy. Recommend enabling deterministic sampling only for very-high-traffic tenants.
- Cost calculation: token_cost_estimate is best-effort using the model-variant cost profile; if a route switches model mid-window we emit an averaged cost and add a 'note' column.

We can expose a signed URL for the CSV and a small Console modal to create thresholding rules that bind to route_id + metric. Notification hooks can use existing webhook/email integrations.

I'll add a short tech note and a sample schema attachment. Estimated effort: 4 engineer-days to wire the aggregation + signed URL + threshold storage; 6 UX days for the Console pieces (if we ship a simple modal). If EdgeScale wants hourly exports and strict p99 correctness for low-traffic routes, double the infra effort.

— Dylan
Staff Software Engineer, Infra Metrics
attachments: sample_export_schema.csv
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Export for per-route cost/latency + alert thresholds

Thanks Dylan — this aligns with what I expected. Proposed product plan (MVP):

Scope (week 1–2):
- Deliver daily CSV export (signed URL) with the columns Dylan listed
- Add 'Export history' card in Console -> Insights that lists the last 30 exports with download links
- Basic threshold modal: route selector + metric dropdown (tokens, token_cost_estimate, p95, p99) + value + webhook/email target

Out of scope for MVP:
- Hourly exports, per-request raw logs, or multi-tenant rollups (Phase 2)

Owners and timeline:
- Infra (Dylan): aggregation job + signed URL endpoints (ETA 4 business days)
- UX/Frontend (Kimberly): modal + export history list + onboarding copy (ETA 6 business days)
- Product (Marissa): acceptance criteria, sample CSV (I attached a mock), and QA steps (ETA 2 business days)

I'll prepare a short PRD and a mock image for the Console flow — attaching the mock and the thresholding proposal. Jonas — can you confirm EdgeScale is OK with daily exports and the averaged cost behavior for routes that change models mid-window?

— Marissa
Product Manager, Observability
attachments: route_breakdown_v1.png, mof_threshold_proposal.md
From: Priya Reddy <priya@edgescale.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Export for per-route cost/latency + alert thresholds

Thanks — that plan sounds reasonable and gets us over the procurement bar for now. A couple of clarifications before we lock: 

1) Daily export is fine, but can you add a column 'model_switch_note' when a route changes model mid-window so our billing team can reconcile?
2) For the threshold notifications, can we have rule-level tags so our on-call can filter only the rules they own?

If you can confirm yes on both, procurement will accept the proposed language and we'll proceed to contract signature next week. I appreciate the detailed scope and the quick turnaround.

— Priya
Director of Engineering, EdgeScale
